comments: Closing this as I believe https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/105259 addressed the issue.

review_comments: The ordinary locks like `lock (Instrument.SyncObject)` allow reentrancy. This should not lead to a deadlock. This description of the problem does not make sense to me.

My guess is that the deadlock you have observed is A-B B-A dead lock between the `Instrument.SyncObject` and the static constructor lock. It is hard to tell for sure without seeing stacktraces of the deadlock. I believe these must be multiple threads involved. I do not think that this can deadlock when everything is executing on a single thread.

Yeah it looked like inverted lock ordering between static constructor and sync object:
![deadlock](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fa90a3b2-aa7c-486f-b800-b0d4652c4de9)

I believe the fix addresses the issue but the comment description doesn't match.

> My guess is that the deadlock you have observed is A-B B-A dead lock between the `Instrument.SyncObject` and the static constructor lock. It is hard to tell for sure without seeing stacktraces of the deadlock. I believe these must be multiple threads involved. I do not think that this can deadlock when everything is executing on a single thread.

I can share dump with you, but you are correct.

> the comment description doesn't match.

Submitted #105539 to delete the wrong comment and simplify the fix.

`RuntimeHelpers.RunClassConstructor` is reflection API. It works, but it is unnecessary overhead. It is not great that it will be called for every Publish.

A more efficient way to ensure static constructor trigger is a dummy Initialize method. We do that for example here: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/54e15cb81d84fae6760b90287468b09250f63e8c/src/libraries/Common/src/Interop/Unix/System.Net.Security.Native/Interop.Initialization.cs#L35-L38
Is Publish hot? By the code it looked to me it is more like `register` and is called once for every kind of Meter, is it?
Publish() is called once per instrument, likely 10-100 times in a run of typical web service process. I don't consider it hot.

I've been thinking about it and this seems OK - I didn't come up with another place where the MeterListener static constructor would be a problem. In the future if we did discover any more it might be worthwhile to move the runtime metrics initialization out of the static constructor and instead do it as a lazy initialization within the MeterListener instance constructor.
Yes, we can consider moving the initialization later out of the static constructor.
